tagline: Powering Progress with Integrated Energy Solutions
hero_kpi_rationale: Hydrocarbon production is the master KPI of the upstream sector and a direct driver of revenues and cash flow. Shell, through its global position and integrated portfolio, depends heavily on this volume to generate value, especially with the ARC Resources acquisition which accelerates its growth toward 4% CAGR through 2030.

kpis.name: Hydrocarbon production
kpis.explanation: Daily quantity of oil and gas produced, converted in barrels of oil equivalent.
kpis.description: The ARC Resources acquisition immediately adds 370 kboe/d of combined production, positioning Canada as a strategic core for Shell with access to Montney basin assets with low carbon intensity.
kpis.signal: 4% CAGR growth through 2030 via ARC Resources acquisition

kpis.name: LNG volumes (liquefied natural gas)
kpis.explanation: Total volume of liquefied natural gas produced and sold each year.
kpis.description: Shell is the world's largest LNG supplier, with a strong position in Asia and North America.
kpis.signal: Shell maintains its position as global LNG leader with stable capacity

kpis.name: Free cash flow
kpis.explanation: Cash generated after capital expenditures, used for dividends and shareholder returns.
kpis.description: FCF is used for dividends, share buybacks and strategic investments in energy transition.
kpis.signal: Sustained growth despite crude price volatility

kpis.name: Capital expenditures (upstream and refining)
kpis.explanation: Annual spending to develop fields, refineries and infrastructure.
kpis.description: Capex supports ARC integration and development of Montney basin assets with top quartile carbon intensity.
kpis.signal: Capex increasing to support post-ARC acquisition growth

kpis.name: Adjusted operating margin (EBITDA)
kpis.explanation: Adjusted profit margin (EBITDA) relative to revenue.
kpis.description: The margin reflects the resilience of the integrated business model despite hydrocarbon price volatility.
kpis.signal: Improvement driven by better downstream performance and operational discipline

kpis.name: Reserves life (R/P ratio)
kpis.explanation: Number of years that current reserves can be produced at the current rate.
kpis.description: The addition of Montney basin reserves via the ARC Resources acquisition significantly extends production visibility for Shell.
kpis.signal: Healthy reserves life, strengthened by ARC's long-duration Montney basin assets

kpis.name: Total assets
kpis.description: Total assets extracted from yfinance over the last 4 years.
kpis.signal: Total assets of €370.35 billion in latest year

kpis.name: Total debt
kpis.description: Total debt extracted from yfinance over the last 4 years.
kpis.signal: Total debt of €75.64 billion in latest year

kpis.name: ARC strategic repositioning
kpis.explanation: Major capital reallocation toward integrated high-return, low-carbon assets via ARC Resources acquisition.
kpis.description: Shell repositions its portfolio via the ARC Resources acquisition, accessing Montney basin assets with top quartile low carbon intensity and long-term duration.
kpis.signal: Strategic repositioning toward high-return, low-cost, low carbon intensity Montney assets

kpis.name: Renewables and low-carbon capex
kpis.explanation: Annual investments in renewable energy, carbon capture and low-carbon technologies.
kpis.description: Shell adjusts its low-carbon strategy to focus on high-return, long-duration projects, integrating ARC's low carbon intensity Montney assets.
kpis.signal: Strategic reduction of renewables capex in favor of high-return long-duration assets

kpis.name: Dividend Per Share
kpis.explanation: Montant total versé en dividendes par action sur l'année fiscale.

kpis.name: Capital Returned to Shareholders
kpis.explanation: Total annuel : dividendes versés + rachats d'actions (treasury).
kpis.description: Cumulative dividends + share buybacks (2021-2025) in billions USD.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.explanation: Part du bénéfice net redistribuée. >80 % = potentiellement non soutenable.

risks.title: Dependence on crude oil and natural gas prices
risks.score_rationale: Risk explicitly cited in first position in forward-looking statements (page 11) as a major factor affecting future operations. Intensive language: 'could cause those results to differ materially'. Trend stable but structural. Critical weight for the entire exploration-production and refining portfolio.

risks.title: Energy transition and declining hydrocarbon demand
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly mentioned page 11: 'pace of the energy transition' and page 90: 'Shell and the energy transition'. Language of commitment and ambition: 'net-zero emissions 2050'. Rising trend: increasing structural risk. Major strategic weight affecting long-term portfolio and R&D investments.

risks.title: Geopolitical risks and international sanctions
risks.score_rationale: Cited page 11: 'risk of doing business in developing countries and countries subject to international sanctions' and page 11: 'Russia-Ukraine war and the conflict in the Middle East'. Direct and specific language. Rising trend since 2022. Significant weight for operations in unstable zones.

risks.title: Regulatory and tax risks related to climate
risks.score_rationale: Mentioned page 11: 'legislative, judicial, fiscal and regulatory developments including tariffs and regulatory measures addressing climate change' and pages 228-240: 'Emission schemes and related environmental plans'. Anticipatory language. Rising trend with CSRD and ETS24. Increasing weight for compliance and operating costs.

risks.title: Cybersecurity and critical IT risks
risks.score_rationale: Cited page 11: 'significant cyber security, data privacy or IT incident' and page 28 (Item 16K Cybersecurity disclosure). Alert language: 'significant'. Rising trend with increasing digitalization. High weight for critical infrastructure operational continuity.

risks.title: Increased competition and market share loss
risks.score_rationale: Cited page 11: 'loss of market share and industry competition'. Moderate but explicit language. Rising trend with emergence of new renewable energy players. Significant weight for Marketing and Renewables segments.

risks.title: Exploration and production operational risks
risks.score_rationale: Mentioned page 11: 'drilling and production results', 'reserves estimates' and pages 52-60 (detailed Upstream section). Technical and cautious language. Trend stable but structural. Major weight for 50% of portfolio (Upstream + Integrated Gas).

risks.title: Environmental risks and asset decommissioning
risks.score_rationale: Cited page 11: 'environmental and physical risks, including climate change' and pages 135-137 (Environment section) and note 25: 'Decommissioning and other provisions'. Legal obligation language. Rising trend with aging assets. Significant weight for accounting provisions (page 275).

ai_positioning.summary: No significant mention of artificial intelligence in the 20-F 2025 report or April 2026 6-K.
